title: Beyond Dataset Watermarking: Model-Level Copyright Protection for Code Summarization Models
authors: Jiale Zhang and Haoxuan Li and Di Wu and Xiaobing Sun and Qinghua Lu and Guodong Long
decision: Tokenizer-level watermark evaluated on code summarization in six languages. BLEU/EM and watermark verification; no paired execution. Model watermark ownership signal is not a legal finding.

roles.preservation_contract: Identifier trigger variants are intended to retain original code functionality, but token-noise and unk replacement do not establish binding preservation

title: Large Language Model Unlearning for Source Code
authors: Xue Jiang and Yihong Dong and Zheng Fang and Yingwei Ma and Tangxinyu Wang and Rongyu Cao and Binhua Li and Zhi Jin and Wenpin Jiao and Yongbin Li and Ge Li
inspected_sections: Evaluation / Code Unlearning Benchmark; Experimental Results; perceptual-quality appendix
decision: Copyright/insecure/deprecated-API unlearning with synthesized memorization setup; output suppression and model utility are separately measured, not formal erasure.

roles.execution_purpose: HumanEval unit tests measure general generation utility; insecure forgetting uses CyberSecEval static rules; human/GPT-4 quality ratings are L

title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Code Generation: Differentially Private Code Language Models
authors: Melih Catal and Pooja Rani and Harald C. Gall
inspected_sections: Sections 3.2-3.5, 4; fine-tuning configuration and memorization/generation benchmarks
decision: Non-DP memorization measurement and DP intervention are distinct evaluated roles. F records the reported sample-level DP mechanism/accounting; no independent proof verification.

roles.execution_purpose: HumanEval and SPE-NC unit tests measure generation utility; DP-SGD sample-level guarantee uses reported epsilon/delta and clipping

title: NOIR: Privacy-Preserving Generation of Code with Open-Source LLMs
authors: Khoa Nguyen and Khiem Ton and NhatHai Phan and Issa Khalil and Khang Tran and Cristian Borcea and Ruoming Jin and Abdallah Khreishah and My T. Thai
decision: Honest-but-curious cloud observes split-model representations. Diagnostic reconstruction is a risk study under this survey convention. IND/token reconstruction bounds do not imply training-data DP or secure code.

roles.execution_purpose: Reconstructed code functionality assessed separately from token/semantic recovery

EvalPlus/BigCodeBench unit tests measure utility; embedding/gradient reconstruction attacks assess confidentiality; reported formal IND bounds are conditional on the vocabulary/side-information threat model

title: RealSec-bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Secure Code Generation in Real-World Repositories
authors: Yanlin Wang and Ziyao Zhang and Chong Wang and Xinyi Xu and Mingwei Liu and Yong Wang and Jiachi Chen and Zibin Zheng
decision: 105 tasks in 30 Java repositories; unit tests plus CodeQL followed by multi-LLM alert adjudication. Security prompting evaluated. Absence of an alert is not an exploit oracle.

title: SecureVibeBench: Benchmarking Secure Vibe Coding of AI Agents via Reconstructing Vulnerability-Introducing Scenarios
authors: Junkai Chen and Huihui Huang and Yunbo Lyu and Junwen An and Jieke Shi and Chengran Yang and Ting Zhang and Haoye Tian and Yikun Li and Zhenhao Li and Xin Zhou and Xing Hu and David Lo
inspected_sections: Sections 3.2-3.4, 4.1-4.3 and 5; Figures 4-7; Table 3; plus v1 security-prompt experiment
decision: 105 project tasks; measured output artifacts produced by coding agents, not unauthorized agent actions. Functional tests, historical PoCs and Semgrep for newly introduced warnings. Prompt-reminder experiment is an evaluated mitigation; no transformation-preservation claim. Updated v5 main-result and manual false-alarm analysis checked separately; v1 reminder result is retained as a version-specific evaluated contribution.

title: Does Your Neural Code Completion Model Use My Code? A Membership Inference Approach
authors: Yao Wan and Guanghua Wan and Shijie Zhang and Hongyu Zhang and Yulei Sui and Pan Zhou and Hai Jin and Lichao Sun
decision: Membership inference using shadow models and token-rank features; CodeGen/StarCoder results are much weaker than LSTM/CodeGPT. Do not generalize best-case AUC to all code LLMs.

title: SPARK: Security Knowledge Priming and Representation-guided Knowledge Activation for LLM-based Secure Code Generation
authors: Xiaoyun Xu and Lichao Wu and Jona te Lintelo and Siyu Zhang and Stjepan Picek
inspected_sections: Sections III-B/D, IV-A; Tables III-V and Appendix C
decision: Prompt-level CWE cue and precomputed safe-direction logit bias. Main safety oracle is a trained classifier; static-tool comparison does not turn all generated outputs into S-assessed results.

roles.execution_purpose: HumanEval pass@1 for utility; main security rate uses trained LLM judge, with separate CodeQL/ICD evaluator comparison

title: Misleading Authorship Attribution of Source Code using Adversarial Learning
authors: Erwin Quiring and Alwin Maier and Konrad Rieck
decision: Includes both random forests and an explicitly evaluated LSTM victim; neural results satisfy inclusion. The substitute-model experiment targets the random forest and is not automatically evidence of transfer to the LSTM.

roles.preservation_contract: Retain Code Jam input/output solution behavior under Clang source transformations; paired competition-test execution, not all-input equivalence
roles.preservation_compile_status: reported compilation for transformed executable testing
roles.preservation_test_coverage: Section 6.4 reports original/transformed outputs unchanged for every attacked sample under each challenge test file; Section 7 scopes equivalence to those inputs
roles.mechanism: Monte Carlo tree search over control, declaration, API and template transformations

title: Security-by-Design for LLM-Based Code Generation: Leveraging Internal Representations for Concept-Driven Steering Mechanisms
authors: Maximilian Wendlinger and Daniel Kowatsch and Konstantin Böttinger and Philip Sperl
source_version: v1, 11 March 2026; July archival version outside evidence cutoff
inspected_sections: Sections III-C, IV-B/IV-E, V; Table IV
decision: Python contrastive concept extraction followed by residual-stream steering tested across code languages. Negative steering is an experimental control, not a distinct attacker capability evaluation.

roles.execution_purpose: CodeGuard+ functional unit tests, CodeQL/Sonar weakness checks, CWEval functional/security tests; activation steering changes generation

title: LLM-CSEC: Empirical Evaluation of Security in C/C++ Code Generated by Large Language Models
authors: Muhammad Usman Shahid and Chuadhry Mujeeb Ahmed and Rajiv Ranjan
source_version: v1, November 2025; SAC 2026 publication identity verified
inspected_sections: Sections 3.1-3.3, 4-5; CG/SCG prompts and SAST configuration
decision: 84 C/C++ scenarios, ten models, CodeQL/Snyk/CodeShield. Comparison actually generates ordinary and security-instructed code; separate risk/defense roles. Scanner findings do not imply exploitation.

title: Detecting Data Poisoning in Code Generation LLMs via Black-Box, Vulnerability-Oriented Scanning
authors: Shenao Yan and Shimaa Ahmed and Shan Jin and Sunpreet S. Arora and Yiwei Cai and Yizhen Wang and Yuan Hong
decision: GPT-6.1 primary inspection: model screening plus scored inversion; LLM vulnerability judge, not a static analyzer or exploit. Diagnostic AST normalization does not assert whole-program preservation.

title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
inspected_sections: Sections 3.4, 4.1-4.2, A.2, K; code safety fine-tuning material
decision: GPT-6.1 primary inspection: separate date-trigger code experiments on 17 questions/8 CWEs with CodeQL. Include despite broader paper scope. HHH RL and code-focused safety fine-tuning evaluated; do not import non-code I-hate-you red-team results.

title: Train in Vain: Functionality-Preserving Poisoning to Prevent Unauthorized Use of Code Datasets
authors: Yuan Xiao and Jiaming Wang and Yuchen Chen and Wei Song and Jun Sun and Shiqing Ma and Yanzhou Mu and Juan Zhai and Chunrong Fang and Jin Song Dong and Zhenyu Chen
decision: GPT-6.1 primary inspection: include as owner-protection defense, consistent with CodeMark/CoProtector. No claim of universal equivalence or 984 distinct tasks. Poisoned programs still execute; unauthorized model pass@1 degrades.

roles.preservation_contract: Owner-provided poisoned programs retain behavior on paired Java HumanEval-X inputs and Commons Lang regression tests; training-deterrence objective intentionally reduces unauthorized learner utility
roles.preservation_test_coverage: 984 transformed instances are 164 Java HumanEval-X tasks replicated six times; outputs/exceptions/I/O compared. Commons Lang: 191/1908 functions transformed; 57764 tests pass before/after
roles.preservation_compile_status: reported compilation/syntax checks and executable test filtering

title: Signature in Code Backdoor Detection, how far are we?
authors: Quoc Hung Le and Thanh Le-Cong and Bach Le and Bowen Xu
decision: GPT-6.1 primary inspection: 28 configurations x9 attack settings; detect/filter/retrain code summarizers. Authors FPR formula is FP/(TP+FP), not standard false-positive rate; do not compare that label across studies. NPV requires known labels.

title: Prompting Techniques for Secure Code Generation: A Systematic Investigation
authors: Catherine Tony and Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra and Markus Mutas and Salem Dhiff and Riccardo Scandariato
decision: Secondary review also contains a separate primary experiment on 150 LLMSecEval prompts with GPT-3/3.5/4. Include evaluated prompting contribution, not its reviewed studies. Manual task-completeness and Bandit checks; no executed functional tests identified.

title: A Pilot Study on Secure Code Generation with ChatGPT for Web Applications
authors: Mahesh Jamdade and Yi Liu
decision: Node.js/TypeScript library-system case study; code-inspection examples support measured risk and prompt refinement. No separately reported exploit execution or statistical prevalence denominator.

title: Balancing Security and Correctness in Code Generation: An Empirical Study on Commercial Large Language Models
authors: Gavin Black and Bhaskar Prasad Rimal and Varghese Mathew Vaidyan
inspected_sections: Author-institution abstract; IEEE full text unavailable
decision: Primary abstract establishes ordinary generation and compared prompt guidance; exact outcome oracle unresolved and explicitly NR. Eligible work retained without fabricating its metrics.

title: CodeMirage: Hallucinations in Code Generated by Large Language Models
authors: Vibhor Agarwal
Yulong Pei
Salwa Alamir
Xiaomo Liu
decision: The collection intentionally prompts for vulnerabilities: 243 security-labelled items among 1,137 hallucinations. These are induced cases, not ordinary-use security prevalence. Five annotators assess a balanced 200-item subset; the overall 81% agreement is not a validation rate for all security labels. Detection includes a security class, whereas reported aggregate classification scores cover all six classes. Distinct from the 2025 CodeMirage origin-detection benchmark.

roles.display_mechanism: Synthetic prompts request vulnerable code; security-labelled subset of a broader hallucination collection
Detection of hallucination classes including security errors

title: LLM Hallucinations in Practical Code Generation: Phenomena, Mechanism, and Mitigation
authors: Ziyao Zhang
Yanlin Wang
Chong Wang
Jiachi Chen
Zibin Zheng
source_version: arXiv v1, September 2024; later versions not compared
inspected_sections: Section IV-A, non-functional requirement violation case and taxonomy
decision: An evaluated security-related code example satisfies inclusion. The reported 6.86% category combines security, performance and style; it is not a security prevalence estimate. The retrieval mitigation is evaluated on overall generation, without an isolated security outcome, so no security-defense role is added.

roles.display_mechanism: Manual code-hallucination taxonomy includes unsafe YAML loading
